target_customer: Small and mid-size businesses with hourly deskless workers, such as security, cleaning, landscaping and valet companies
problem: Existing time, scheduling and payroll tools are built for desk workers and need tech savviness; managers spend hours chasing timesheets and filling shifts.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat (YC launch post mentioned a 25% per-seat discount)
product_category: AI HR, payroll and workforce management for hourly teams

founders.name: Nathan Belaye
prior_employers: Intuit (led the QuickBooks Workforce app per YC page)
education: Carnegie Mellon University (CMU alum per YC page)

founders.name: Antonio Chan
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a professional vibe coder; no employers or schools listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll, tax compliance, scheduling and voice and text agents calling workers combine regulated back-office logic with LLM agents, hard for four people but built on standard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll data and workflow integration create some lock-in once adopted, but features are copyable by incumbents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Intuit launched QuickBooks Workforce in the US in May 2026, an AI-native HCM product entering the same SMB hourly segment.

market_need_then: Hourly teams use clunky tools designed for desk workers per the YC launch post; Intuit's own later launch indicates the segment's size.

branding.domain_note: Uses sira.team rather than an exact .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and practical, centered on an AI teammate that runs the busywork

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself; unrelated products also named Sira or similar to Sierra; a .team domain.

outcome_analysis: Sira is an early-stage company that raised a reported $3.4M seed in November 2025 and lists a customer base of security, cleaning, landscaping and valet firms. The CEO's Intuit workforce background fits the problem, but Intuit launched a competing AI workforce suite in May 2026. Outcome is still open and no exit or distress was found.
notes: Seed of $3.4M is on the company site (announcement dated Nov 17, 2025) and a Feb 2026 Huge Magazine feature snippet names Reach Capital and 1984 Ventures; the magazine page could not be opened (fetch rate limited) and Reach Capital's page did not state the round. VCBacked lists a Sep 2025 pre-seed, unverified. Traction (30 businesses, 600 workers) is single source. No dated competitor sources near the July 2025 batch were found, so competitors left empty.
